mainTopic: Bailees' liability for an ox, and how much guarding exempts the owner of a תם or a מועד: the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a ברייתא on bailees of a goring ox: whose view does it follow? It cannot fully match רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה. רב הונא בר חיננא says it follows רבי אליעזר on guarding and רבי יהודה on the שוכר. אביי says it follows רבי מאיר, in רבה בר אבוה's version where the two opinions about the שוכר are switched. רבי אלעזר then rules that a שומר חנם pays if the ox damages others but not if it is injured. רבא explains that the guard knew the ox was a gorer and took responsibility only for protecting others. A new משנה follows with three views on an ox that was tied or locked in properly and still did damage: רבי מאיר says both תם and מועד are liable, רבי יהודה says only the תם is liable, and רבי אליעזר says only slaughter counts as guarding. The גמרא explains how רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה read the פסוקים, including the rule that a ריבוי after a ריבוי comes to limit. It also brings רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says lesser guarding is enough for both. Finally, רב אדא בר אהבה says רבי יהודה exempts only the מועד half, and the גמרא uses רב's rule about the right and left horns to show that רב disagrees with him.

steps.title: If the teaching follows רבי מאיר, the renter should be exempt too
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who says a שוכר is like a שומר חנם, it should have listed the שוכר as exempt together with the שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If it is like רבי מאיר,] who says a renter is like an unpaid guard, then the teaching should say: 'except for an unpaid guard and a renter!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its first challenge. If this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, its wording does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא exempts only the שומר חנם. רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר has the same level of responsibility as a שומר חנם. So by his view, the שוכר should have been exempted as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A renter: someone who pays to use an animal or item
An unpaid guard (bailee), who has the lightest responsibility
Is like, is compared to
Let it teach: the text should have said

phrases.english: who says: a renter is like an unpaid guard,
phrases.notes: The sentence started just before this line with: 'If it is like רבי מאיר.'

phrases.english: let it teach: 'except for an unpaid guard and the renter!'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: שׂוֹכֵר כְּשׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם דָּמֵי, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question, begun just before this, about whose view the ברייתא follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר equates the שוכר with the שומר חנם, so the שוכר should share the exemption. The ברייתא does not list it.

steps.title: If the teaching follows רבי יהודה, all should be exempt from ransom for a forewarned ox
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, the שוכר fits, but the ברייתא should then also have said that all the bailees are exempt from כופר when the ox is מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is like רבי יהודה, who says a renter is like a paid guard, let it teach: 'except for an unpaid guard; and with forewarned oxen, all of them are exempt regarding ransom!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, רבי יהודה, and shows that his view does not fit the ברייתא either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a שוכר is like a paid guard, so leaving it off the exempt list fits him. But רבי יהודה also holds that a מועד ox needs only light guarding. Light guarding should then free every bailee from כופר, and the ברייתא does not say that.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guard, who has more responsibility
Forewarned oxen: ones known to gore
Ransom: the payment for a person killed by an ox
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions fail for different reasons. With רבי מאיר, the problem is the שוכר. With רבי יהודה, the problem is the מועד ox and כופר.

phrases.english: And if it is like רבי יהודה,
who says: a renter is like a paid guard,
let it teach: 'except for an unpaid guard,
and with forewarned oxen, all are exempt regarding ransom!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: שׂוֹכֵר כְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר דָּמֵי – נִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the challenge. Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה fits the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's light-guarding rule for a מועד ox should exempt everyone from כופר. The ברייתא does not say this.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חיננא: רבי אליעזר on guarding, רבי יהודה on the renter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that only slaughtering truly guards an ox. On the שוכר, it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר, who says the only real guarding for an ox is a knife. And about the renter, he holds like רבי יהודה, who says a renter is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חיננא answers the double challenge by combining two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that no guarding helps for a dangerous ox except slaughtering it. So a light-guarding exemption from כופר never applies, and that removes the problem from step 2. On the שוכר, the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, so the שוכר rightly is not exempt, which removes the problem from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Guarding, safeguarding
A knife: meaning slaughtering the ox
He holds like

phrases.english: רב הונא בר חיננא said:
Whose is this? It is רבי אליעזר,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין לוֹ שְׁמִירָה אֶלָּא סַכִּין;
phrases.english: who says: it has no guarding except a knife;
phrases.notes: In plain words, the only way to make a goring ox safe is to slaughter it.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְעִנְיַן שׂוֹכֵר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and regarding a renter, he holds like רבי יהודה,
who says: a renter is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both parts of the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a combination of opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow either רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי אליעזר on guarding and רבי יהודה on the שוכר.

steps.title: אביי: It is רבי מאיר, with the opinions switched
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, using רבה בר אבוה's version. In that version, רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a paid guard and רבי יהודה says he is like an unpaid guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really it is like רבי מאיר, following how רבה בר אבוה switched the opinions and taught: How does a renter pay? רבי מאיר says: like a paid guard. רבי יהודה says: like an unpaid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, different answer. He keeps the ברייתא with רבי מאיר by using a version in which the two opinions are swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר treats the שוכר as a paid guard, so leaving the שוכר off the exempt list fits. רבי מאיר does not hold רבי יהודה's light-guarding rule for a מועד ox, so the כופר problem does not come up either.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeping the original suggestion
Switches: reverses who said what
How does he pay? What level of responsibility does he have?

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רב הונא בר חיננא says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר on guarding plus רבי יהודה on the שוכר. אביי says it follows רבי מאיר, in the version where the opinions about the שוכר are switched.
steps.confusionAlert: In אביי's version the names are reversed. Here רבי מאיר is the one who says a שוכר is like a paid guard.

phrases.english: אביי said: Really, it is like רבי מאיר,
and as רבה בר אבוה switched it and taught:
How does a renter pay?
רבי מאיר says: like a paid guard,
רבי יהודה says: like an unpaid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב הונא בר חיננא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Using a version with the opinions switched
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר is like a שומר חנם, so the ברייתא cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר is like a paid guard, so the ברייתא fits him.

steps.title: An unpaid guard is liable for the ox's damage but not for its injury
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that an unpaid guard who received an ox pays if it damages, but is exempt if it gets injured.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: If someone handed his ox to an unpaid guard, and the ox caused damage, the guard is liable. If the ox was injured, the guard is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר about an ox given to a שומר חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling splits the guard's responsibility in two. He is responsible when the ox damages others, but not when the ox itself gets hurt. This split is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid guard, someone watching an item for free
Handed over, gave into someone's care
It caused damage (to others)
It was damaged (it got hurt itself)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
If one handed his ox to an unpaid guard,
if it caused damage, he is liable;
phrases.notes: "He" here is the guard, not the owner.

phrases.english: if it was injured, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about bailees, after the earlier discussion of which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unpaid guard is liable when the ox damages others, and exempt when the ox is injured.

steps.title: How can the guard be liable one way and exempt the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי אלעזר means. Either the guard accepted responsibility or he didn't, and either way the two halves should match.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What is the case? If he accepted responsibility for guarding the ox, he should be liable even when it gets injured! And if he did not accept responsibility for guarding it, he should be exempt even when it causes damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's split ruling. It argues that both halves should come out the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge sets up two options. If the guard took on the job of guarding, he should answer for everything, including the ox getting hurt. If he did not take on the job, he should answer for nothing, including the damage it causes. Either way, a split ruling seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
He accepted upon himself, took on the responsibility
Guarding regarding its damages

phrases.english: They said: What is the case?
If he accepted upon himself the guarding of its damages,
then even if it was injured, he should also be liable!

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ שְׁמִירַת נְזָקָיו –
phrases.english: And if he did not accept upon himself the guarding of its damages,
then even if it caused damage, he should also be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 5 by asking what case could fit it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's split between damage caused and injury suffered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Responsibility is all-or-nothing. Either the guard accepted guarding, which makes him liable in both cases, or he didn't, which makes him exempt in both cases.

steps.title: The guard knew it was a gorer, so he only took responsibility for others
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the guard did accept responsibility, but only for what he expected. He knew the ox gores, so he expected it to hurt others. He never thought others would hurt it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, he did accept responsibility for guarding it. But here we are dealing with a case where he knew the ox was a gorer. Normally, a person in that case agrees to stop it from going and hurting others. But he never considered that others would come and hurt it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by explaining exactly what the guard agreed to. It depends on what he knew about the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting responsibility does not have to cover everything. It covers what the guard had in mind. Because he knew the ox was a gorer, he took on the job of protecting others from it, but not of protecting the ox from others. That explains the split.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (holding on to the first option)
Here, what are we dealing with? (introduces a specific case)
A gorer, an ox known to gore
The ordinary way of things, what is normally assumed
Brought it up into his mind, considered it

steps.whatToRemember: A guard is responsible for what he had in mind when he took the job. Knowing the ox was a gorer, he took on stopping it from hurting others, not protecting it from being hurt.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a guard's responsibility can be partial. It follows what he realistically expected when he took the object.

phrases.english: Rava said: Really,
he did accept upon himself the guarding of its damages,
and here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where he recognized that it is a gorer.
And the ordinary way of things is:

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אָזֵיל אִיהוּ וּמַזִּיק אַחֲרִינֵי – קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that it should not go and damage others, this he accepted upon himself;
that others will come and damage it, itself,
he did not bring into his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו שְׁמִירַת נְזָקָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the guard knew the ox was a gorer, so his accepted responsibility was limited.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting responsibility for guarding must cover every kind of loss, both damage and injury.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guard accepted only what he expected: stopping a known gorer from damaging others, not protecting it from others.

steps.title: משנה: An ox tied or locked in properly that gets out and damages
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי מאיר says that if the owner tied or locked in his ox properly and it still got out and damaged, he is liable, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the owner tied his ox with reins and locked the gate in front of it properly, and it still got out and caused damage, he is liable whether it is a תם or a מועד. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses whether proper guarding frees the owner from liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the owner guarded the ox the proper way, רבי מאיר holds him liable. This applies both to a תם (an ox not yet known to gore) and to a מועד (one known to gore). The משנה presents this as רבי מאיר's view, so other opinions may follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Reins, a rope or strap for tying an animal
Locked (the gate) in front of it
Properly, in the fitting way
An ox not yet established as a gorer
An ox established as a gorer, after warnings

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If its owner tied it with reins
and locked the gate before it properly,
and it got out and caused damage,
whether innocuous or forewarned, he is liable,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the discussion of the unpaid guard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, an owner who tied or locked in his ox properly is still liable for its damage, whether it is a תם or a מועד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a well-guarded תם is liable but a מועד is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with רבי יהודה. If the owner tied or locked up his ox properly and it still did damage, a תם is liable but a מועד is exempt, because the פסוק about a מועד speaks of an owner who did not guard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a תם is liable, and a מועד is exempt. This is because the פסוק says 'and its owner has not guarded it,' and this ox was guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יהודה's view, which disagrees with רבי מאיר from the last step. רבי יהודה splits the two kinds of oxen: a תם is liable and a מועד is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר held that the owner is liable for both a תם and a מועד, even with proper guarding. רבי יהודה points to the פסוק about a מועד, which makes the owner liable only when he 'did not guard it.' Here the owner did guard it, so for a מועד he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that has not yet built up a pattern of goring; its owner pays half the damage.
An ox that has been warned about (it has gored several times); its owner pays full damage.
'And its owner has not guarded it.' This is the פסוק about a מועד.
Guarded, kept safe.

steps.confusionAlert: This looks backwards: the more dangerous ox (מועד) gets the easier law! The גמרא will explain in steps 13–14 why רבי יהודה reads the פסוקים this way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: an innocuous ox (tam) is liable,
phrases.notes: He is still talking about the case from the last step: the owner tied or locked up the ox properly, and it got out anyway.

phrases.english: and a forewarned ox (mu'ad) is exempt;
as it is said: "and its owner has not guarded it"
and this one was guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תָּם חַיָּיב, וּמוּעָד פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the משנה, disagreeing with רבי מאיר's view in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the ox was guarded properly, a תם is liable and a מועד is exempt, based on 'ולא ישמרנו בעליו'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the only real guarding is a knife
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that no amount of tying or locking up is enough. The only guarding that works is slaughtering the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: there is no guarding for it except a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion, the strictest one. רבי אליעזר says that no guarding ever exempts the owner, except slaughtering the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argued about whether proper guarding is enough. רבי אליעזר says that for a goring ox, no guarding is ever enough. If the ox is alive and it gores, the owner pays.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife. Here it means slaughtering the ox.
'It has no guarding except...' The only thing that counts as guarding.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
it has no guarding except a knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ שְׁמִירָה אֶלָּא סַכִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, strictest opinion to the משנה's מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No guarding exempts the owner of a goring ox; only slaughtering it counts.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on a properly tied ox that gored: רבי מאיר says both תם and מועד are liable. רבי יהודה says תם is liable and מועד is exempt. רבי אליעזר says only a knife counts as guarding.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source and logic behind רבי מאיר's view that both a תם and a מועד are liable even after proper guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why רבי מאיר holds his view. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view seems to go against the פסוק 'ולא ישמרנו', which hints that guarding should help. So the גמרא needs to show how he reads the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here.
'What is the reason?' A request for the logic or source of a view.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה, starting with the first opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning and פסוק-reading behind רבי מאיר's ruling that both a תם and a מועד are liable despite proper guarding.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: both a תם and a מועד need superior guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that oxen are normally not guarded. So the Torah's making a תם liable teaches that it needs at least lesser guarding. The פסוק about a מועד teaches that it needs superior guarding. Then he learns a תם from a מועד, so a תם also needs superior guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that ordinary oxen are not assumed to be guarded. The Torah said a תם is liable, which teaches that it needs at least lesser guarding. Then the Torah said 'and has not guarded it' about a מועד, which teaches that it needs superior guarding. And he learns goring of a תם from goring of a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and explains רבי מאיר's reasoning step by step, using the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since oxen are normally left unguarded, the Torah's ruling that a תם is liable only shows that a תם needs lesser guarding. The extra words 'ולא ישמרנו' for a מועד show that a מועד needs more: superior guarding. Because both פסוקים talk about 'goring,' רבי מאיר links them, so a תם also needs superior guarding. That is why tying it with reins is not enough for either one.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary oxen, the way oxen usually are.
Presumed to be guarded.
Lesser guarding, like tying with reins.
Superior guarding, like a strong locked door.
'The Merciful One.' It means the Torah.
He learns (one case from another).

phrases.english: He holds: ordinary oxen
are not presumed to be guarded;
and the Torah said a tam is liable
teaching that it needs (at least) lesser guarding,

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״וְלֹא יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ״ גַּבֵּי מוּעָד
phrases.english: then the Torah said "and has not guarded it" regarding a mu'ad
teaching that it needs superior guarding;
and he learns goring of a tam
phrases.notes: Both פסוקים use the word 'gore,' so רבי מאיר links them. Whatever a מועד needs, a תם needs too.

phrases.english: from goring of a mu'ad.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: סְתָם שְׁווֹרִים – לָאו בְּחֶזְקַת שִׁימּוּר קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Oxen are normally unguarded. A תם's liability teaches lesser guarding, and 'ולא ישמרנו' teaches superior guarding for a מועד. A גזירה-style link between the two 'goring' פסוקים carries the superior-guarding requirement over to a תם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, for רבי מאיר, simple guarding like reins never exempts the owner of either type of ox.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the Torah demands superior guarding twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that oxen are normally given some lesser guarding. So the Torah's making a תם pay anyway shows that a תם needs superior guarding. The פסוק about a מועד then says again that it needs superior guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that ordinary oxen are assumed to be guarded. The Torah said a תם pays, which teaches that it needs superior guarding. Then the Torah said 'and has not guarded it' about a מועד, which teaches that one must give it superior guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי יהודה's reasoning, starting from the opposite assumption about ordinary oxen. This sets up the key rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, oxen normally get lesser guarding. If a תם still makes its owner pay, then lesser guarding is not enough; it needs superior guarding. But then the פסוק about a מועד says the same thing again, and that repeat leads to the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He will pay.
'That one must do for it.' That one must provide (the guarding).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds: ordinary oxen
are presumed to be guarded;
the Torah said a tam pays,
teaching that it needs superior guarding;

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא ״וְלֹא יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ״ גַּבֵּי מוּעָד
phrases.english: then the Torah said "and has not guarded it" regarding a mu'ad
teaching that one must give it superior guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: סְתָם שְׁווֹרִים – בְּחֶזְקַת שִׁימּוּר קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same פסוקים, now for רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since oxen normally get lesser guarding, a תם's liability shows that it needs superior guarding. The 'ולא ישמרנו' פסוק for a מועד seems to repeat the same requirement.

steps.title: A double inclusion limits: a מועד needs only lesser guarding
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah demanded superior guarding twice, this is a 'ריבוי after a ריבוי,' which comes to limit. So the Torah removes the need for superior guarding from a מועד; lesser guarding is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is an inclusion after an inclusion, and an inclusion after an inclusion comes only to limit. So the פסוק limits (it removes) the requirement of superior guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יהודה's reasoning with a rule for reading the Torah. This explains why he exempts a well-guarded מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים that both teach the same extra requirement are read as limiting instead of adding. So for a מועד, the superior-guarding requirement is removed, and lesser guarding is enough to exempt the owner. A תם still needs superior guarding, which is why רבי יהודה holds a תם is liable and a מועד is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion after an inclusion: two extra teachings that say the same thing.
To limit or exclude.
The פסוק limited (it took something out).

steps.confusionAlert: 'מיעט הכתוב לשמירה מעולה' does NOT mean a מועד needs superior guarding. It means the superior-guarding requirement is taken away from a מועד, so lesser guarding is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: both תם and מועד need superior guarding (oxen are normally unguarded, and 'goring' links the two). רבי יהודה: a תם needs superior guarding, but a מועד needs only lesser guarding, because a ריבוי after a ריבוי comes to limit.

phrases.english: This is an inclusion after an inclusion,
phrases.notes: The Torah demanded superior guarding twice: once by making a תם pay, and again with 'ולא ישמרנו'.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט
phrases.english: and an inclusion after an inclusion comes only to limit
so the verse excluded (the need for) superior guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי, וְאֵין רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the double requirement laid out in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using the rule that a ריבוי after a ריבוי comes to limit, רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as removing the superior-guarding requirement from a מועד. So a מועד given lesser guarding is exempt, while a תם is liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the whole reason רבי יהודה's surprising ruling works: the more dangerous ox gets the easier guarding requirement.

steps.title: Why not learn the תם from the מועד through the word 'goring'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines someone asking: the Torah uses 'goring' for both a תם and a מועד, so shouldn't a תם also get away with lesser guarding?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us compare 'goring' said about a תם with 'goring' said about a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to רבי יהודה's view. It sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה, a מועד needs only lesser guarding, but a תם still needs superior guarding. The objection is that the Torah uses the same word 'goring' for both, and that kind of word link usually makes the two cases follow the same rule. If so, the תם should need only lesser guarding too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a possible objection
Goring
Comparing two cases because the Torah uses the same word in both

phrases.english: And if you will say:
goring for a תם, goring for a מועד
phrases.notes: He means: the same word 'goring' is used for both, so let the תם follow the מועד's easier rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome of step 14, where only the מועד got the leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that a תם still needs superior guarding
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shared word 'goring' should link the two cases, so the מועד's leniency should carry over to the תם.

steps.title: The word 'it' limits the leniency to the מועד
steps.stepSummary: The Torah wrote 'and he did not guard IT,' which teaches that the leniency is for this ox (the מועד) and not for the other (the תם).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah limited it by writing 'and he did not guard it': for this one, and not for another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The Torah's wording 'ולא ישמרנו' ('guard IT') blocks the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'it' points only to the מועד. So the easier rule of lesser guarding stays with the מועד and does not pass to the תם, even though both use the word 'goring'. A clear limit in the פסוק overrides the word comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah limited it
And he did not guard it
For this one and not for another

phrases.english: But the Torah limited it:
'and he did not guard it'
for this one, and not for another.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מועד, and 'another' is the תם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a limiting word in the פסוק that blocks the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'goring' would make the תם follow the מועד's leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ישמרנו' ('it') keeps the leniency for the מועד only.

steps.title: Isn't that phrase needed for the basic rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'ולא ישמרנו' is needed to teach the basic rule that an owner who didn't guard is liable, so it can't also teach a limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this phrase is needed for the basic negative statement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 16. The phrase already has its own job, so it seems we can't learn the limit from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא ישמרנו' plainly tells us the owner pays when he did not guard the ox. If the phrase is used up teaching that, nothing is left over to teach 'this one and not another.'

keyTerms.meaning: But it is needed for (something else)
A negative statement: here, 'did NOT guard'

phrases.english: But it is needed for the negative statement!
phrases.notes: He means the plain message: if the owner did not guard it, he must pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'ולא ישמרנו' to limit the leniency
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A phrase needed for its plain meaning cannot also be used to teach an extra limit.

steps.title: The extra 'it' is what teaches the limit
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah only wanted the basic rule, it could have written 'ולא ישמור.' The added 'it' teaches 'this one and not another.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the Torah should have written 'and he did not guard.' Why does it say 'and he did not guard it'? To teach: for this one and not for another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The basic rule comes from the main word, and the limit comes from the extra 'it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא ישמור' alone would be enough to teach that the owner pays. The added ending 'נו' ('it') is not needed for that. So it teaches something new: the leniency of lesser guarding belongs only to the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the Torah write
And he did not guard (without 'it')

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a מועד needs only lesser guarding, and the extra 'it' in 'ולא ישמרנו' keeps that leniency away from a תם.

phrases.english: If so, let the Torah write
'and he did not guard.'
Why 'and he did not guard it'?
For this one and not for another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and confirms the answer of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק: the base word teaches the rule, and the extra letters teach the limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole phrase is used up by the basic rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ולא ישמור' gives the basic rule, and the extra 'נו' limits the leniency to the מועד.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: lesser guarding is enough for both
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a fourth opinion. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that both a תם and a מועד are exempt if the owner gave lesser guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, whether it is a תם or a מועד, if the owner guarded it with lesser guarding, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new opinion. Lesser guarding is enough for any ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the most lenient view so far. רבי יהודה required superior guarding for a תם, but רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says even a תם needs only lesser guarding.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (in a ברייתא)
Lesser, basic guarding
Exempt from paying

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
Whether a תם or a מועד
that he guarded with lesser guarding
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new opinion after finishing the explanation of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lesser guarding exempts the owner for both a תם and a מועד.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds this way. It sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know which steps of the earlier reasoning he accepts and which he rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and logic for exempting even a תם with lesser guarding.

steps.title: He agrees with רבי יהודה and then compares the תם to the מועד
steps.stepSummary: He agrees with רבי יהודה that a מועד needs only lesser guarding, and he uses the shared word 'goring' to give the תם the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יהודה, who said that lesser guarding is enough for a מועד, and he learns 'goring' of a תם from 'goring' of a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason. He starts from רבי יהודה's view and then makes the comparison that רבי יהודה rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts that the 'double ריבוי' brings the מועד down to lesser guarding. Unlike רבי יהודה, he does use the 'goring' comparison to carry that leniency over to the תם. He must not learn a limit from 'ישמרנו' the way רבי יהודה did in steps 16 to 18.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like
It is enough for it
And he learns (one case from another)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views. רבי מאיר says both need superior guarding. רבי יהודה says a מועד needs lesser and a תם needs superior. רבי אליעזר says only slaughter works. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says lesser guarding is enough for both.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is not the same person as רבי אליעזר from step 10. רבי אליעזר is the strictest view, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the most lenient.

phrases.english: He holds like רבי יהודה, who said:
for a מועד, lesser guarding is enough,
and he learns goring of a תם from goring of a מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He accepts רבי יהודה's leniency for a מועד and extends it to a תם through the shared word 'goring'.

steps.title: Lesser guarding only removes the extra payment of a מועד
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that רבי יהודה exempts only the מועד part of the ox. The תם part, which is half-damage, still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: רבי יהודה only exempted the 'warned' part of the ox. The 'innocent' part stays in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה limits רבי יהודה's rule that a מועד ox needs only lesser guarding. If the owner guarded it only in the lesser way, he is still liable for the half-damage that any תם would pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מועד ox pays full damage, which is like a תם's half plus an extra half. According to רב אדא בר אהבה, lesser guarding frees the owner only from the extra half. The basic half stays, as if the ox were a תם that was not guarded well enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'warned' side of the ox: the extra half-payment that comes from being מועד
The 'innocent' side of the ox: the basic half-damage that every goring ox pays
Exempted
Stays in its place, still applies

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה lets the owner of a מועד ox go completely free with lesser guarding. According to רב אדא בר אהבה, he still pays half-damage.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Rabbi Yehuda did not exempt
anything except its forewarned element,
phrases.notes: He means the extra half that a מועד pays beyond what a תם pays.

phrases.english: but the element of innocuousness remains in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: לָא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא צַד הַעֲדָאָה שֶׁבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows how רבי יהודה's lesser-guarding rule for a מועד works in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יהודה, lesser guarding of a מועד exempts only the extra half. The half-damage of the תם side still applies.

steps.title: An ox warned for its right horn is not warned for its left
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that an ox's מועד status for goring with the right horn does not carry over to the left horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: An ox that is warned about its right horn is not warned about its left horn.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new rule: being מועד for one horn does not make the ox מועד for the other horn. This sets up the גמרא's question about whose opinion רב is following.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מועד status is tied to the specific way the ox has shown its habit. If it gored three times with its right horn, a goring with its left horn is still treated like a תם's goring.

keyTerms.meaning: Right horn
Left horn
A forewarned ox with an established habit of goring

phrases.english: Rav said: An ox forewarned for the right horn
is not forewarned for the left horn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מוּעָד לְקֶרֶן יָמִין – אֵינוֹ מוּעָד לְקֶרֶן שְׂמֹאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new statement that the גמרא will test against the opinions about guarding
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מועד status for the right horn does not extend to the left horn.

steps.title: Whose opinion fits רב's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רב follows. Under רבי מאיר the rule seems unneeded for guarding. Under רבי יהודה, as רב אדא בר אהבה explained him, even the right horn already has both a תם side and a מועד side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Whose view is this? If it follows רבי מאיר, he says both a תם and a מועד need superior guarding! If it follows רבי יהודה, why mention the left horn specifically? Even the right horn has both an innocent side and a warned side!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fit רב's rule into the argument about guarding. Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה seems to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי מאיר, every ox needs superior guarding, so in this discussion about guarding there is no reason to separate the two horns. Under רבי יהודה, רב seems to be pointing out an ox with a mix of תם and מועד. But according to רב אדא בר אהבה, a right horn that is מועד already has a תם side, so there is no need to bring in the left horn.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
Superior guarding
Why specifically this case?
The warned side of the ox

phrases.english: They said: In accordance with whom?
If in accordance with Rabbi Meir,
doesn't he say: both an innocuous ox and a forewarned ox
require superior guarding!
If in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
why specifically the left horn?
Even with the right horn as well,
it has an element of innocuousness,
and it has an element of being forewarned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule by trying to match it with each opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that a right-horn מועד is not מועד for the left horn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided problem. Under רבי מאיר the rule adds nothing about guarding. Under רבי יהודה, as explained by רב אדא בר אהבה, the right horn alone already shows both sides, so mentioning the left horn is unnecessary.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יהודה but disagrees with רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב follows רבי יהודה but does not accept רב אדא בר אהבה's limit. For רב, an ox has both a תם side and a מועד side only in a case like the two horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Really it follows רבי יהודה, and he does not agree with רב אדא בר אהבה. This is what he means: it is in a case like this that you find in an ox both an innocent side and a warned side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying רב follows רבי יהודה and rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's view. The explanation of what רב means starts here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, a horn that is מועד is fully מועד, so lesser guarding exempts that horn completely, with no leftover תם half. The only way to find a mixed ox is with two different horns: the right horn is מועד and the left horn is a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (holding on to the original idea)
He does not hold this view
In a case like this
You find

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation of רבי יהודה is not accepted by everyone. רב understands רבי יהודה differently.

phrases.english: They said: Actually, it is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה;
phrases.english: and he does not hold like Rav Adda bar Ahava;
and this is what he is saying:
It is in a case like this
that you find in it an element of innocuousness and of being forewarned,
phrases.notes: He means an ox that is מועד with one horn and a תם with the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge by picking רבי יהודה and setting aside רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption from step 22 that the challenge depended on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone following רבי יהודה accepts רב אדא בר אהבה's view, so the right horn alone has both sides
steps.terutzMaskana: רב does not accept רב אדא בר אהבה's view. A mixed תם and מועד ox is found only when the two horns have different status.
